text: Error handling in doeff. A failure is handled like everything else: with an effect and a handler.
First, run itself. It gives back what the program returns, as it is: here, the string DOEFF.
When the program raises, run raises the same exception. There is no wrapper around either.
To keep a failure as a value, doeff has two kinds of result. Ok holds a value. Err holds an exception.
Ok is true and Err is false, and both match by pattern.
Try is an effect. app yields Try, with the sub-program it wants to attempt.
The try handler catches the effect, and runs parse count inside itself.
int raises on the text "not a number". The handler catches the exception and wraps it in Err.
Then it resumes k with that Err. app goes on: it logs the failure and returns zero.
Without the try handler in the stack, Try is unhandled. It is a handler like any other.
Try keeps three promises when it meets other effects.
One: no rollback. The Put before the failure stays, so counter is one.
Two: when the failure passes through Local, Local still restores the environment. key is outer again.
Three: Try inside Try keeps both layers. You get Ok of Ok, or Ok of Err.
Err keeps the exception, and the exception keeps its traceback.
Its frames lead from inside the try handler, through boom, down to load, where the error was raised.
Failures in doeff: Try asks, a handler answers with Ok or Err, and your code decides what comes next.
